subject: BrightLeap integration — technical summary, owners, and next actions
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Shah <anika@brightleaphealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: BrightLeap integration — recap and proposed owners

Thanks again for the call today, Anika — great context on your production goals for triage summarization and the two-step reranker flow. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize the action items, proposed owners, and a technical checklist so we have alignment before we book the follow-up architecture session.

High level notes (from call)
- Workload: low-latency summarization + embeddings-based retrieval + rerank (approx. 300 reqs/min peak, 50 qps steady).
- Data posture: PHI-adjacent (must stay within BrightLeap VPC for inference, no bridging of raw PHI to Redwood-hosted S3).
- Desired flow: internal API -> VPC endpoint (Private) -> Redwood runtime (pinned model) -> structured JSON output with tool-calling hooks for post-processing.

Primary owners
- BrightLeap network/security: Anika (network) + Karen (security)
- BrightLeap engineering: Samir (integration lead)
- Redwood: Mina (sales/AM owner), Ben (SE - SDK + auth), Jordan (solutions - routing, VPC config), Marissa (CS - rollout/okrs)

Immediate technical checklist (please confirm):
1) Private connectivity: VPC endpoint(s) or PrivateLink equivalent + IP allowlist for the endpoint(s). BrightLeap to provide CIDR and preferred endpoint model.
2) Egress & DNS: outbound egress from Redwood to BrightLeap? We discussed connector pattern — BrightLeap will accept inbound to a VPC endpoint; Redwood needs to support optional DNS override and TLS SNI.
3) Auth: short-lived mTLS client certs for inference calls OR token-based mutual auth via customer-managed auth proxy (we discussed both).
4) SDK + structured output: Ben to propose SDK snippet for structured JSON (tool calling keys + schema).
5) Embeddings & reranker: local reranker hosted by Redwood with embedding storage in BrightLeap-managed VPC (or encrypted store) — confirm whether BrightLeap prefers embeddings replicated to their VPC.

Attachments: I uploaded an initial onboarding playbook and a quick network diagram. Please review and annotate.

Next steps
- BrightLeap: share CIDR ranges, desired hostname(s) for VPC endpoint, and whether you prefer mTLS or token bearer with a short-lived proxy. (Due: Fri 2027-09-10)
- Redwood: Ben/Jordan to prepare an SDK-auth example and a minimal VPC endpoint config doc. (Target: Mon 2027-09-13)
- Schedule: propose a 60-min architecture walkthrough the week of 9/13 — I’ll send a Doodle after we get availability.

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad

Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLeap integration — recap and proposed owners

Thanks Mina — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 
- CIDR: we will provide two /24 ranges for the endpoint (internal only).
- mTLS vs tokens: security prefers mTLS for inference calls into our VPC; tokens okay for non-PHI metadata requests.
- Embeddings: we'd prefer embeddings stored in our controlled bucket (encrypted) with Redwood writing via an agreed replication path; can you outline the write pattern (push vs pull) in the next doc?

We can target 9/14 for the architecture walkthrough; Samir and Karen will join. I'll attach our security checklist in a follow-up.

-Anika

--
Anika Shah
Head of Cloud Ops, BrightLeap Health
anika@brightleaphealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: BrightLeap integration — recap and proposed owners

Hi Anika / team — quick tech notes and an SDK sketch to unblock decisions: 
- SDK/auth: Our SDK supports two auth modes for private deployments:
  * mTLS: Redwood issues short-lived client certs (valid 24h) via your CA integration (you can rotate). Calls present client cert during TLS handshake to your VPC endpoint.
  * Token + proxy: Redwood mints short-lived tokens; BrightLeap runs a verification proxy that validates token and forwards with internal auth.
- Structured output: we can enforce a JSON schema at the model response layer. Example snippet: { "type": "object", "properties": { "summary": {"type": "string"}, "actions": {"type": "array"} } }
- Embeddings writes: Redwood can push embeddings to a customer-managed S3-compatible endpoint over HTTPS. We will sign writes and can encrypt in transit. Optionally, we can host embeddings and provide pull replication.

I’ll attach a short sample SDK call and an mTLS handshake flow diagram to the internal playbook draft. Jordan and I can put together a minimal VPC endpoint CloudFormation snippet if you want.

Ben

--
Ben Carter

ben@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 12:41:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: BrightLeap integration — recap and proposed owners

Adding routing and network specifics based on the checklist: 
- VPC endpoint model: recommend interface endpoint (PrivateLink) per region. Each endpoint will be associated with the subnets you designate; we will provide the service name and TLS cert chain for validation.
- IP allowlist: we will accept either (a) a BrightLeap-managed allowlist of Redwood egress IPs or (b) mutual TLS where IP allowlisting is less strict. Given PHI-adjacent constraints, mTLS is preferred.
- DNS: if you want a short internal FQDN (api-inference.brightleap.internal), we can support SNI and optional DNS override in our client.
- Ports: only 443 for TLS. Health checks from Redwood to your endpoint will come from ephemeral addresses; we can pin them if you need static healthcheck IPs.

Proposed minimal CloudFormation snippet (summary):
- create network interface endpoints in selected subnets
- attach security group that allows 443 from Redwood cert-validated clients
- route tables unchanged (interface endpoint)

I’ll bring the CFN snippet to the call on 9/14.

Jordan

Thanks Jordan — that level of detail is helpful. A couple of items from our infra lead: 
- We'll share the /24s and the desired internal FQDN by EOD 9/10.
- For embeddings we prefer push (Redwood writes to our encrypted bucket). Can you confirm the s3-compatible interface and that writes will be TLS 1.2+?
- On the mTLS flow: can Redwood's certs be anchored to our internal CA? We need a short note we can hand to security to explain rotation and expiry.

We'll plan for 9/14 10:00am PT for the architecture walkthrough — calendar invite to follow.

Samir
